Docs

Build with MDL

The core language is small: sections create structure, Markdown creates content, dot elements create controls, and attributes add detail.

Contents

  • Basics
  • Projects
  • Build

Basics

MDL uses indentation to nest sections. A hero section becomes a .mdl-hero element, and a card section becomes a .mdl-card element.

Sections

Use names like page, topbar, nav, grid, card, form, details, and footer.

Inline elements

Use dot elements such as .badge(beta), .href@href(/docs)(Docs), and .input@type(email).

Attributes

Add explicit attributes with @id(value), @class(value), @required, or @submit(handlerName).

Project layout

A complete MDL website is just a folder with pages, CSS, optional scripts, and mdl.json.

  1. Configure

    Set pages, output, styles, scripts, title, and local preview port in mdl.json.

  2. Author pages

    Put each .mdl page under the configured pages folder. Nested folders become nested routes.

  3. Keep assets nearby

    Store images under assets and reference them from CSS or page content.

Build and preview

Run ../../bin/mdl serve inside this project for live preview, or ../../bin/mdl build to compile static output into dist.

What gets generated?

The build creates one HTML file for each MDL page and writes a bundled stylesheet at dist/app.css.

How do scripts bind?

Event attributes such as @click(showDocsBasics) are compiled into data attributes. The generated runtime imports scripts/site.js and calls exported functions by name.

Want to see the components in context?

Browse the examples page for repeated cards, comparison layouts, and a contact workflow.
